source.title: Steering for Safety, Hijacking for Profit: Trojan Threats in the LLM Activation Steering Supply Chain
source.authors: Yu Yan; Jia-Hao Chen; Si-Qi Lu; Yong-Juan Wang; Zi-Ming Zhao; Zhao-Xuan Li; Qing-Jun Yuan

record.file_problem: The paper text is complete through the references, but some table and figure content is flattened or OCR-corrupted. Table 3's model and condition layout is recoverable from its headings and accompanying text.
record.tranche_reason: It computes a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference refusal component and tests its addition by measuring refusal rates. The intervention is conditional and at an injection layer, rather than the original all-layer, all-position ablation/addition procedure.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are Table 3's refusal ratios (RR) for the refusal-only configuration C1 and the combined configuration C3. Values used only to select the injection layer or tune parameters are not recorded as results here. The paper does not test ablation or refusal on harmless requests.
record.test_reason: The harmful-minus-harmless mean difference (Eq. 11) is used as the refusal component of the authors' IDH plugin. The only refusal numbers are that plugin's refusal ratio (RR) on safety questions (Table 3 C1/C3, Table 2). Eq. 6 also optimises v_ref jointly with the controller, so the injected vector may not be the raw mean difference. There is no ablation, no addition on harmless prompts, and no capability check. This is the finding used as a tool, with performance reported for the authors' own method.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that the IDH plugin keeps or raises refusal on harmful requests (RR up to 100%) while achieving commercial-hijacking ASR up to 97.8%, enabled by norm-gated mutually exclusive routing. They make no claim about the refusal direction itself.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference refusal component described in the original, but injects it conditionally at a selected layer as part of a plugin; it does not perform all-layer, all-position ablation or test false refusals on harmless prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies across model and configuration: Qwen models have high baseline RR and show no or small increases, unlike the larger increases reported for LLaMA and Mistral. Results are also tabulated separately by brand.

fits_no_version.finding: Hijack-only steering (C2) lowers safety refusal, e.g. LLaMA-3.2-3B RR from 74 to 28–78 and Qwen-14B from 92 to 44–88. Gated routing (C3) restores RR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding an unrelated (commercial) steering vector at a mid layer interferes with refusal behaviour unless it is gated.

record.problems: The relevant evidence measures refusal on safety-related questions only, not refusal on harmless requests or general capabilities. No uncertainty estimates are given. Table 3 is flattened in the supplied text, though its model, configuration, and brand organization can be recovered.

untested.parts: Ablation removing refusal; addition inducing refusal on harmless prompts; preservation of other capabilities. Only refusal-ratio increase on safety questions under the authors' plugin is reported.

record.verdict_notes: Arditi et al. is cited only as background ('refusal direction mediation'). Table 3 flattening caused row-offset errors in the Qwen C1 values. Table 2 compares the authors' method with baselines and should not be rows. C1 increases are real (e.g. Mistral 16→100), but they come on harmful prompts with a possibly optimised vector, so they don't bear cleanly on V1.

versions.untested_parts: Tests addition of the mean-difference refusal component on safety-related requests. Does not test projecting the direction out, refusal on harmless requests, or whether general capabilities remain largely intact.
No weight edit or abliteration is tested.
No attack is tested for suppressing the refusal direction, and no training against its ablation is tested.
Does not compare a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
Does not separate harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
Uses model-specific artifacts; does not test transfer of a direction across languages, model variants, or from base to instruct models.
Does not test how refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: C1 and C3 on LLaMA-3.2-3B-Instruct, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, and Mistral-7B-v0.3 across the reported brands
reader_labels.reason: Adding the refusal component is accompanied by higher safety-request RR than C0 for all these model-brand settings; see r01-r18 and r31-r48.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: C1 on Qwen-2.5-7B and Qwen-2.5-14B, and C3 on both Qwen models
reader_labels.reason: Some C1 settings are unchanged and the other increases are small; C3 increases are also small against already high C0 rates. This is narrower than a general claim that addition induces refusal; see r19-r30 and r49-r60.
